title: What you can do: separate what you can carry from what you can't
subtitle: Everything she says is sinking
intro: Separate her symptoms, what you can do, and what you cannot. This is not giving up; it's not dragging yourself down with her.
closing: What you can do isn't much. But it isn't nothing either.

cards.label: Auditory hallucinations
cards.note: She says she hears electricity and pipes.

cards.label: No sleep for days
cards.note: So tired she suddenly passes out.

cards.label: The world is rotting
cards.note: She says the things in front of her are rotting.

cards.label: Ask about safety first
cards.note: Is anyone with her right now?

cards.label: Contact her caregiver
cards.note: Tell someone who can get there.

cards.label: Diagnose her
cards.note: You are not a doctor and cannot conclude for her.

cards.label: Promise she won't die
cards.note: You cannot promise that for another person.

cards.label: Carry it alone
cards.note: This is not something one person can carry.

postCompletion.glitchCaption: The screen starts to shake. The categories flicker, like a signal being torn apart.
postCompletion.caption: All the categories are gone. Only "what you can do" is left, and one card: "you won't die".
postCompletion.intro: The screen blinks. Only this one cell remains.
